mistakes.title: Forgetting the quotes around text
mistakes.explanation: Beginners assume print(Hello) works because it reads naturally.
mistakes.traceback:
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
NameError: name 'Hello' is not defined
mistakes.fix: Wrap text in quotes so Python knows it is text, not a variable name.

mistakes.title: Using a variable before assigning it
mistakes.explanation: Beginners may forget to assign a value to a variable before trying to use it, thinking that declaring it is enough.
mistakes.traceback:
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
NameError: name 'score' is not defined
mistakes.fix: Make sure to assign a value to the variable before using it in print().

mistakes.title: Incorrect variable name format
mistakes.explanation: Beginners often try to start variable names with numbers or use spaces, not realizing the rules for valid names.
mistakes.traceback:
File "<stdin>", line 1
    1st_variable = 10
    ^
SyntaxError: invalid decimal literal
mistakes.fix: Start variable names with a letter or underscore, and avoid spaces.
